terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: portable twin-head halogen work light on a folding telescopic tripod
motionPotential: the legs fold and the mast telescopes in the real object, but the prop ships in its deployed pose as a rigid body - it is placed, not operated
objectClass.notes: The twin halogen work light dragged out for night roadworks, building sites and market set-up. It is the only PHYSICS-ENABLED prop in this lighting set at 7 kg, which HALVES its collider part ceiling from 4 to 2.

reasoning: THREE drawn parts, against a medium default of two. The ceiling was raised to 3 on the asset with the reason recorded, because a splayed tripod cannot be expressed in two: the three legs radiate from a common apex so no single swept spine covers them, and the repetition emitter places instances around a circle WITHOUT tilting them, so a radial system would build three vertical legs and not a tripod.
The split is chosen so each part is one continuous spine: two legs as a single V through the apex, the third leg continuing straight up into the mast, and the crossbar with both heads as a third.
The lens faces are a vertex-colour band on the head member, because two materials is the whole allowance.
It stands on the floor, so the pivot is at base-center.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate; sub-structure carried as localFeatures because each component costs one of only four draw calls.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Three legs at 120 degrees splaying to r 0.45.
A flat pad at each leg end.
Two mast sections with a clamp collar at the junction.
Two trapezoid housings spanning nearly the whole leg splay.
A four-bar frame around each glazed face.
A box and knob at the mast head with the yoke bar below it.
A pane behind each bezel, the only cool bright surface on the prop.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Leg splay is read off the plate at roughly 0.36 m from the axis at the feet for a 1.30 m apex; the real stand is adjustable and this is one deployed pose. Confidence 0.7.
The small round lamp on top of the plate's example (probe band 0, luma 95) is NOT built: it is a third head on a prop already at a raised draw-call ceiling. Confidence 0.8.
The telescopic mast's clamp collars and the legs' folding hinges are not built - thin hardware the budget cannot carry. Confidence 0.85.
The far side of the tripod is not in the single view; the third leg's position is inferred from three-fold symmetry. Confidence 0.8.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: three legs splayed at 120 degrees, none vertical
two distinct heads readable, tilted forward
all three feet at or below y 0.02
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not build the legs with a radial repetition system; it does not tilt its instances and would produce three vertical legs.
Do not split the two heads into two components; the ceiling is already raised.
Do not lift the orange toward grey - it is the most saturated prop in the set and clears the hole gate comfortably.
Do not declare a fold or telescope pivot; the prop ships deployed.
Do not let the feet hover above y 0.
qualityContract.depthRationale: THREE components across two material layers. Seven micro-feature groups: the splayed tripod, the telescoping mast, the foot pads, the twin heads, their bezel frames, the junction box and the recessed glass.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be about 0.80 x 1.75 x 0.80 m within the asset's 10% tolerance.

featureReviewTargets.name: Three splayed legs
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Three legs radiating from a common apex at 120 degree spacing, each tilted outward. Three vertical legs fail - that is exactly what the repetition emitter would have built and why this prop is authored as two swept members instead.

featureReviewTargets.name: Two tilted heads on a crossbar
featureReviewTargets.criteria: TWO orange trapezoid housings, each with a four-bar bezel frame and a glazed face visible behind it. White blobs fail, and so does a solid bezel plate -- it swallows the glass and the heads read as plain blocks.

featureReviewTargets.name: Safety orange and lens faces
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Strong saturated orange near the measured 128-154 with bright lens faces. This is the most saturated prop in the set and needs no lift to clear the hole gate.

featureReviewTargets.name: Stands on its three feet
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Three splayed legs with flat foot pads, and a convex collider over the whole stand. This is the kit's only DYNAMIC lighting prop at about 7 kg, so it has to topple believably rather than sink.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: safety orange 128-154 at saturation 0.66-0.78 against pale lens faces - the widest chroma of any prop in this set.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as three named parts. Not articulated and not breakable, though it IS the one physics-enabled prop in this lighting set at 7 kg.

assumptions: Leg splay is 0.36 m at the feet for a 1.30 m apex, read off the plate; the real stand is adjustable and this is ONE deployed pose.

A three-legged stand's footprint is a TRIANGLE, so it cannot be 0.80 m in both plan axes. The feet are placed at 30/150/270 degrees and sized so the declared 0.80 m is met along X; the Z extent is 0.70 m, 12% under the declared depth. Widening the stand to reach 0.80 in Z would take the X extent to 0.92 and overshoot instead.
The small round lamp on top of the plate's example is NOT built: a third head on a prop already at a raised draw-call ceiling.
The telescopic clamp collars and the folding hinges are not built - thin hardware the budget cannot carry.
The far side of the tripod is inferred from three-fold symmetry; the single view does not show the third leg clearly.
The prop ships in its DEPLOYED pose as a rigid body. The real stand folds and telescopes, but a level places this, it does not operate it, so no pivot is declared for either motion.
The lens faces are opaque and NOT emissive.
physics.enabled is true at 7 kg, which HALVES the collider part ceiling from 4 to 2 - the tightest collider budget in this lighting set.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits on the ground plane at the centre of the tripod's footprint, so the prop stands on a floor with no offset.

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 0.849 x 1.695 x 0.745 m against the declared 0.8 x 1.75 x 0.8 -- 6% over on width, 3% under on height, 7% under on depth, all inside tolerance. A three-leg tripod cannot be square in plan (x = 1.732r, z = 1.5r), so the declared square footprint is an approximation and r 0.45 is the splay that lands both extents inside 10%.
silhouette.symmetry: three-fold about the Y axis for the stand; bilateral about the YZ plane for the head bar
silhouette.notes: The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.549 against the declared 0.457 - the closest plate-to-declared agreement in this lighting set, because a portable prop is photographed whole.

componentTree.name: Three splayed legs, feet, telescoping mast and clamp collar
componentTree.topologyRationale: The stand as one merged mesh: three swept legs, three flat feet, a two-section telescoping mast and its clamp collar. They are one fabricated assembly on one material, so the whole stand is one submission -- which matters because the draw-call ceiling here is three.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. Three tubes of r 0.019 from a hub at y 1.02 down to feet at r 0.45 and 120 degrees apart; a lower mast cylinder to y 1.08 and a thinner upper section sliding out of it; a clamp collar at the junction.

localFeatures.description: Three legs at 120 degrees splaying to r 0.45 with a flat foot pad at each end. A THREE-leg tripod cannot be square in plan -- its x extent is 1.732r and its z extent 1.5r -- so the declared 0.8 x 0.8 footprint is an approximation of a hexagonal one, and r 0.45 is the value that lands both extents inside the 10% tolerance.
Two mast sections with a clamp collar where the thinner upper one slides out of the lower. The previous build had a single smooth pole.
A flat pad at each leg end, which is what the stand actually rests on and what makes it read as standing rather than as three sticks touching the ground.

componentTree.notes: Safety orange #c4762a with shadowed castings #a25f20, plus a chipped-paint tile.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Site-painted safety orange carrying its shadowed castings, steel yokes and dark tilt knobs as vertex colours, with chipped paint as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Junction box, knob and the two floodlight heads
componentTree.topologyRationale: The two heads, their bezels, their yokes and the junction box are one material and one submission. At a three-call ceiling on a prop with a separate glass material, that is the only way to keep the lenses on their own material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A junction box and knob at the mast head, a yoke bar, and two 0.265 x 0.205 m trapezoid housings either side at x +-0.215, each with a four-bar bezel frame, a yoke arm and a tilt knob.

localFeatures.description: Two heads sized so the pair spans nearly the whole leg splay, as the plate shows. At 0.19 m each they read as lamps clipped to a stand rather than as the thing the stand exists to carry.

The bezel is a FRAME of four bars, not a plate. As a single box it sat in front of the glass and swallowed it whole, and the heads rendered as plain orange blocks with no lens at all -- which is most of what the previous build got wrong too.
A box and knob at the mast head above the heads, with the yoke bar the heads hang from.

componentTree.notes: Steel yokes #8e9092 and dark tilt knobs #6b5a3c as vertex colours on the same orange material.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Site-painted safety orange carrying its shadowed castings, steel yokes and dark tilt knobs as vertex colours, with chipped paint as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Two glazed faces
componentTree.topologyRationale: Glass is the only non-orange surface on the prop and the brightest thing on it, so it earns the second material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two 0.244 x 0.184 m panes set behind the bezel frames, larger than their openings so the frame grips them.

localFeatures.description: Set INSIDE the bezel rather than flush with its face -- co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight, and a real work light's glass sits behind its frame.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A clear glazed face behind each bezel.

materials.name: Safety orange painted steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: Plate subject mask p20 58,77,83 (the shadowed glass) / p50 194,115,49 (the orange, luma 127) / p80 243,151,8.
The orange renders near 164 and its darkest faces near 90, so the whole range clears gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window and no lift was needed -- unlike this kit's dark green and bronze props.
Four tones on one material because the draw-call ceiling here is three and the glass has to have one of them.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

localOverrides.description: The lens faces as a vertex-colour band over the front of each head (local z 0.16..0.22), authored at #E8E4D6. The generator clones a painted component's material and forces its colour to white, so vertexPaint.baseColor IS the albedo and this is a final colour.
The frame's own tone, carried by the authored albedo rather than a synthesised map.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Roughness 0.58 over a chipped site finish.

evidence: The plate's two lenses are the only cool bright regions on an otherwise wholly orange prop.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.

acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.849 x 1.695 x 0.745 m against the declared 0.8 x 1.75 x 0.8 -- 6% over on width, 3% under on height, 7% under on depth, all inside tolerance. A three-leg tripod CANNOT be square in plan: its x extent is 1.732r and its z extent 1.5r, so the declared square footprint is an approximation of a hexagonal one. r 0.45 is the splay that lands both extents inside 10%; at the first r of 0.395 the depth came out 17% under.

Three swept legs at 120 degrees with a flat foot pad at each end, and a TWO-SECTION telescoping mast with a clamp collar where the thinner upper slides out of the lower. The previous build had a single smooth pole and no feet at all -- the pads are what make it read as standing rather than as three sticks touching the ground.

Two trapezoid housings sized so the pair spans nearly the whole leg splay, as the plate shows, each with a four-bar bezel frame, a yoke arm and a tilt knob, under a junction box and knob at the mast head. The bezel had to become a FRAME: as a single box it sat in front of the glass and swallowed it whole, and the heads rendered as plain orange blocks with no lens -- which is most of what the previous build got wrong too, with two white blobs and no housing, bezel, glass or yoke.

Two material layers. Safety orange #c4762a measured off the plate (p50 194,115,49, luma 127) carrying its shadowed castings, steel yokes and dark tilt knobs as vertex colours, plus a chipped-paint tile -- four tones on one material because the draw-call ceiling here is three and the glass has to have one of them. The orange renders near 164 and its darkest faces near 90, clear of gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so no lift was needed.

A convex hull collider over the whole stand, which is what this prop needs: it is the kit's only DYNAMIC lighting prop, declared at about 7 kg so a player can knock it over, and that declaration halves the collider part ceiling. A box over the splayed legs is what makes it stand and then topple rather than sink.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: The build measures 468 triangles at 3 draw calls, 2 materials and 3 geometries -- AT the draw-call ceiling of three, which is what shaped the component split: the whole stand is one submission and both heads share the junction box's, so the glass can have its own material. Triangles are barely an eighth of the ceiling.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the head bar and the upper legs carry the brightest orange.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black.
No separate rim in the plate.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A light grey backdrop at luma ~225; foreground coverage is 13.4%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot, on the ground at the centre of the footprint. The real stand folds and telescopes, but this prop ships deployed and a level places it rather than operating it; declaring hinge or telescope axes would promise articulation the factory does not build.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. Nothing clips onto a work light; the heads are fixed to their own bar.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
